desc: Brute-force N=4 and N=6: enumerate all 2^{C(N,2)} graphs, compute BFS layers from vertex 1, count connected graphs with equal even/odd distance-parity classes by edge count M; verify against Sample 1 and Sample 2.

Confirm the layer-based characterization: BFS layers L0={1},L1,...,Lk; edges only within a layer or between adjacent layers; every vertex in L_{i+1} has ≥1 neighbor in L_i; condition is sum of even-layer sizes = sum of odd-layer sizes; each valid graph corresponds to exactly one layering.

Design the layer DP: state (u=vertices placed, t=last layer size, b=balance even−odd, p=parity of last layer) → polynomial in x; transition adding layer of size s multiplies by ((1+x)^t −1)^s·(1+x)^{C(s,2)}.
Implement transition polynomials Q_{t,s}(x) mod P.
Implement the DP with numpy vectorization (arrays over (balance, edges) per (u,t,p); convolution via scalar-multiply-and-add slices per Q coefficient).
Extract answer: sum over all states with u=N−1, b=0, any t,p; output answers for M=N−1..N(N−1)/2 mod P.
Validate current implementation against brute force for N=4 and N=6 and Sample 3 (N=10); fix indexing bugs (balance row offset r0, answer slice) — all three samples now match exactly.
Fix int64 overflow risk: chunked k-loop with np.mod every ACCUM_LIM=8 iterations; re-validated Samples 1–3.

Run a final timing check for N=30 (worst case) to confirm it fits within typical time limits; if too slow, apply the balance prune |b| ≤ V−u and/or adaptive mod frequency (mod every max(1, 8e18 // P²) steps).
Optimize Q-precomputation: precompute factorials/inverse factorials up to 435 once and use them for all binomial(tj,m) and binomial(w,m) computations instead of the naive per-m loop with pow().
Final check: run Samples 1–3 end-to-end, confirm N=30 completes within time limit, and verify output format (single line, space-separated, M from N−1 to N(N−1)/2).
